data.title: Dermatitis artefacta — viva
data.summary: Psychocutaneous disorders · 8 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Dermatitis artefacta** (Psychocutaneous disorders)_

**Q1. Classify psychocutaneous disorders (PYQ).**
- Psychophysiological disorders — skin disease worsened by stress (psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, urticaria, acne, alopecia areata, hyperhidrosis)
- Primary psychiatric disorders with skin manifestations — dermatitis artefacta (factitious disorder), delusional infestation (delusional parasitosis), body dysmorphic disorder, trichotillomania, skin picking (excoriation) disorder, neurotic excoriations, acne excoriée, onychophagia, dysmorphophobia, Dhat syndrome
- Secondary psychiatric disorders due to skin disease — depression, anxiety, social phobia (vitiligo, psoriasis, acne, alopecia)
- Cutaneous sensory disorders — glossodynia, vulvodynia, scalp dysaesthesia, chronic pruritus without cause
- Skin side-effects of psychotropic drugs (lithium acne/psoriasis, anticonvulsant SJS, antipsychotic pigmentation)

**Q2. Define dermatitis artefacta (PYQ).**
- Self-inflicted skin lesions produced consciously but with motivation that is unconscious (need for care, attention, escape from stress) — the patient denies self-infliction; a factitious disorder (not malingering, where there is conscious external gain)
- Commonest in adolescent girls and young women; often with borderline personality traits, past trauma/abuse, stress, health-care workers

**Q3. Clinical clues.**
- 'Hollow history' — lesions appear fully formed overnight, vague account, patient unconcerned (la belle indifférence) while family anxious
- Bizarre geometric shapes, straight lines, sharp angulated margins, normal surrounding skin, within reach of the dominant hand (spares the hand used, mid-back spared), unilateral, symmetrical patterns
- Lesion types: excoriations, burns (cigarette, chemical — drip marks), ulcers, purpura (suction, ligature), blisters, panniculitis (injection of foreign material — milk, faeces, oil), dermatitis from caustics, hair pulling, eyelid/lip lesions
- Failure to heal with standard therapy; healing under occlusive dressing (e.g. plaster cast) — diagnostic

**Q4. How do you differentiate dermatitis artefacta, malingering and neurotic excoriations?**
- Artefacta: unconscious motive, denies self-infliction
- Malingering: conscious production for external gain (compensation, avoid work/prison)
- Neurotic excoriations/skin picking: patient admits picking (compulsion), lesions in reachable areas, repeated picking of normal skin or minor bumps

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Vasculitis, pyoderma gangrenosum (pathergy — surgery worsens), contact dermatitis, porphyria, bullous diseases, infections (ecthyma, atypical mycobacteria), panniculitis, Munchausen syndrome by proxy (child), child abuse/non-accidental injury

**Q6. Investigations.**
- Mainly clinical and to exclude organic disease: biopsy (foreign-body granuloma, polarisable material), cultures, patch test; occlusion test (healing under sealed dressing)
- Psychological assessment

**Q7. Management.**
- Non-confrontational, empathetic, long-term relationship with the patient — avoid accusing directly; acknowledge distress
- Symptomatic wound care, occlusive dressings, treat infection
- Joint dermatology–psychiatry (psychodermatology) care: psychotherapy (CBT, dialectical behaviour therapy), treat underlying depression/anxiety/personality disorder — SSRIs, low-dose antipsychotics
- Avoid unnecessary investigations/surgeries; involve family carefully; safeguarding in children

**Q8. Write short notes on delusional infestation (PYQ).**
- Fixed false belief of being infested by parasites/organisms despite no evidence; middle-aged/elderly women; 'matchbox sign' (bringing specimens — lint, skin debris)
- Primary (monosymptomatic hypochondriacal psychosis) or secondary (schizophrenia, depression, dementia, drugs — cocaine, amphetamines, dopamine agonists; organic — B12 deficiency, hypothyroidism, renal failure)
- Treatment: build trust, exclude real infestation and organic causes, antipsychotics — risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole, (pimozide — older, QT prolongation)

## Quick spotter facts
- Bizarre geometric lesions within reach of the dominant hand, 'hollow history' — dermatitis artefacta
- Heals under occlusion

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Psychocutaneous disorders). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
